---
title: "Try it yourself"
subtitle: "Pick a population and a sample size, then watch thousands of averages pile up"
page-layout: full
toc: false
code-tools: false
---

```{=html}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/site.css">
<div class="lp">
<p class="lead" style="margin:0 0 22px">
  Each <b>study</b> picks <b>n</b> values at random from the population and averages them.
  The simulator repeats the study thousands of times and stacks up the averages.
  If the Central Limit Theorem has kicked in, they form the red bell curve.
</p>
<div class="sim">
  <!-- ============ CONTROLS ============ -->
  <div class="panel controls">
    <label class="ctl" for="pop">1 · Population</label>
    <select id="pop">
      <optgroup label="Textbook distributions">
        <option value="normal">Normal (bell curve)</option>
        <option value="die">Six-sided die</option>
        <option value="exponential" selected>Exponential (waiting times)</option>
        <option value="binomial">Binomial (5, 0.1): rare-event counts</option>
        <option value="cauchy">Cauchy (extreme tails)</option>
      </optgroup>
      <optgroup label="Real data">
        <option value="faithful">Old Faithful geyser: minutes between eruptions</option>
        <option value="discoveries">Great inventions per year</option>
        <option value="diamonds">Diamond prices (USD)</option>
        <option value="flights">NYC flight arrival delays (minutes)</option>
        <option value="counties">Midwest county populations</option>
        <option value="rivers">North American river lengths (miles)</option>
      </optgroup>
    </select>
    <div class="hint" id="pop-desc"></div>

    <label class="ctl" for="n-slider">2 · Sample size n <span class="note">(values per study)</span></label>
    <div class="n-row"><div class="n-display" id="n-display">5</div>
      <input id="n-input" type="number" min="1" max="5000" value="5" style="width:110px"></div>
    <input id="n-slider" type="range" min="0" max="1000" value="190">
    <div class="quick" id="quick"></div>

    <label class="ctl">3 · Number of studies (B)</label>
    <div class="seg" id="b-seg">
      <button data-b="1000">1,000</button><button data-b="10000">10,000</button><button data-b="100000" class="on">100,000</button>
    </div>
    <div class="hint" id="b-note">The full study used 100,000.</div>

    <label class="ctl">4 · Standard for “normal enough”</label>
    <div class="seg" id="std-seg">
      <button data-s="strict">Strict</button><button data-s="main" class="on">Main</button><button data-s="lenient">Lenient</button>
    </div>

    <label class="ctl" for="seed">Random seed</label>
    <input id="seed" type="number" value="9426">

    <div class="actions">
      <button class="go" id="run">▶ Run all studies</button>
      <button class="one" id="one">+1 study (watch it)</button>
      <button class="reset" id="reset">Reset</button>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- ============ STAGE ============ -->
  <div class="stage">
    <div class="row2">
      <div class="panel">
        <h3 class="ph">The population</h3>
        <p class="sub" id="pop-sub">Where each value comes from.</p>
        <svg id="pop-chart" viewBox="0 0 460 200"></svg>
      </div>
      <div class="panel">
        <h3 class="ph">One study</h3>
        <p class="sub" id="one-sub">Click “+1 study” to see the n values of a single study and their average.</p>
        <svg id="one-chart" viewBox="0 0 460 200"></svg>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="panel">
      <div class="n-row"><h3 class="ph">The averages of all studies</h3><span class="counter" id="counter">0 studies</span></div>
      <p class="sub">Bars: how many studies got each average. <span style="color:var(--bell);font-weight:700">Red curve</span>: the bell curve the Central Limit Theorem predicts.</p>
      <svg id="hist-chart" viewBox="0 0 960 330"></svg>
      <div class="note" id="hist-note"></div>
    </div>

    <div class="verdict-box idle" id="verdict" aria-live="polite">
      <div class="icon">…</div><div><div class="t">Run the studies to get a verdict</div><div class="d"></div></div>
    </div>

    <div class="score" id="score"></div>

    <div class="row2">
      <div class="panel">
        <h3 class="ph">Q-Q plot</h3>
        <p class="sub">If the averages are normal, the dots follow the straight line.</p>
        <svg id="qq-chart" viewBox="0 0 460 300"></svg>
      </div>
      <div class="panel">
        <h3 class="ph">What the full study found</h3>
        <div class="found" id="found"></div>
        <p class="sub" style="margin-top:12px">The browser uses a different random number generator than R, so results right at
          the threshold can differ slightly. Try n just below and just above the study's answer.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</div>
<script src="assets/simulator.js" defer></script>
```
